turns: Which hubs in the Midwest are most exposed to winter disruption?
results.answer: Minneapolis (MSP) is the most exposed Midwest hub to winter disruption, with a winter score of 48.2. That is moderate, not high. Chicago (39.9) and Detroit (37.4) follow, and both are moderate. Kansas City (33.8) is just inside moderate. Indianapolis (30.7) and Columbus (30.1) are low. MSP is driven by 146.4 freeze days/yr (min temp <= 0 C) and 20.4 days/yr with snowfall >= 1 cm. Chicago has 103.6 freeze days and 18.6 snow days. Detroit has 111.4 freeze days and 17.0 snow days.

turns: Compare Miami and Houston in terms of hurricane and flood exposure.
results.answer: Miami has the higher hurricane/wind exposure, and Houston has far higher flood exposure. On wind, Miami scores 51.9 (moderate) and Houston 43.1 (moderate). Miami's gap comes mainly from FEMA wind declarations: 11 versus 8 over 20 years. Gust days are similar, at 11.8 days/yr with gusts of 60 km/h or more in Miami and 10.8 in Houston. On flood, Houston scores 74.7 (high) and Miami 32.4 (low). Houston has 23.6 days/yr with 25 mm or more of rain, against 9.2 in Miami. It has 4.2 days/yr with 50 mm or more, against 2.2 in Miami. It also has 7 FEMA flood declarations, against 2 for Miami. Houston's overall score is 39.0 (moderate) and Miami's is 22.7 (low).

turns: What percentage of days in Denver last year had snowfall?
results.answer: In 2025, Denver had measurable snowfall (at least 0.1 cm) on 37 of 365 days, which is 10.1% of days. Snowfall of at least 1 cm occurred on 17 days, or 4.7%.

turns: Why is the Dallas hub's weather disruption risk high?
results.answer: Dallas is not rated high. Its composite Weather Disruption Risk Score is 36.5, which is moderate (high starts at 66). The drivers are 16.2 days/yr with at least 25 mm of rain and 3.6 days/yr with at least 50 mm. Heat adds 6.8 points, from 54.6 days/yr above 35 C. Wind adds 9.9 points, partly from 5 FEMA wind declarations over 20 years. Winter adds only 3.5 points.

turns: Which three hubs have the highest overall weather disruption risk?
results.answer: The three highest composite scores are Houston (HOU) at 39.0, Dallas (DFW) at 36.5 and Newark (EWR) at 33.4. All three are rated moderate, so none is high in absolute terms. They only rank highest relative to the rest of the network. Houston is driven by flooding (23.6 days/yr with at least 25 mm of rain) and by FEMA wind declarations (8 in 20 years). Dallas is driven by heavy rain (16.2 days/yr) and heat (54.6 days/yr above 35 C). Newark is driven by FEMA wind declarations (7 in 20 years) and heavy rain (12.2 days/yr). Houston and Dallas are 2.5 points apart, and Dallas and Newark are 3.1 points apart. The tool flags Houston and Newark as close calls with the next hub, so treat the order of HOU and DFW, and of EWR and the hub ranked fourth, as uncertain.

turns: Which hubs face the biggest hurricane risk?
results.answer: Miami has the highest hurricane/wind score in the network at 51.9. That is only moderate, and no hub reaches high (66 or above). Newark (43.3), Houston (43.1) and Dallas (39.6) follow, also moderate. Atlanta is fifth at 26.6, which is low. Miami's score is driven mainly by FEMA hurricane, tropical storm, tornado and wind declarations (11 declarations in 20 years) and by 11.8 days/yr with gusts of 60 km/h or more. Houston has 8 declarations. Newark has 7 declarations and 20.4 gust days/yr. Newark and Houston are a close call (0.2 points apart), so their order is not meaningful.

turns: Where is extreme heat the biggest problem for us?
results.answer: Phoenix (PHX) is the clear heat hotspot. Its heat score is 100 (high), driven by 137.4 days/yr with max temp at or above 35 C. Dallas (DFW) is a distant second at 45.5 (moderate), with 54.6 days/yr above 35 C. Houston (22.3, 26.8 days/yr), Denver (14.8, 17.8 days/yr) and Kansas City (10.0, 12.0 days/yr) are all low. Only Phoenix scores high in absolute terms.

turns: Compare Denver, Minneapolis and Chicago for winter risk.
results.answer: Denver has the highest winter risk of the three at 53.9, then Minneapolis at 48.2 and Chicago at 39.9. All three are 'moderate', so none is 'high' in absolute terms. Denver leads because it has the most freeze days (152.2 days/yr at or below 0 C) and snow days of 1 cm or more (22.4 days/yr). It also has 1 FEMA winter declaration over 20 years. Minneapolis has 146.4 freeze days/yr and 20.4 snow days/yr, with no FEMA winter declarations. Chicago has 103.6 freeze days/yr, 18.6 snow days/yr and 0.6 heavy-snow days/yr. Minneapolis and Denver both have 1.2 heavy-snow days (10 cm or more) per year. No NWS alerts are active at any of the three hubs right now.
